title: IAM delegation scenarios and template policies
content:
Purpose:

This working doc collects practical delegation scenarios, a compact IAM role matrix across Hosted / Dedicated / Private environments, and copy-paste policy templates and SIEM mapping examples that engineering and security can use to implement RBAC v2 and automated evidence collection. It is intended as a pragmatic companion to the formal RBAC design doc (see linked artifacts) and focuses on edge cases that regularly come up during Dedicated/Private onboarding.

Summary of intent and constraints:
- Minimize blast radius: default deny, narrow permission sets, escalate via short-lived sessions.
- Environment differences: Hosted uses Redwood-managed control plane resources; Dedicated mixes customer-dedicated GPU clusters + Redwood control plane; Private can be fully customer-hosted with local KMS and audit sinks.
- RBAC v2 model: permission sets are fine-grained actions (e.g., inference.run, model.deploy, workload.admin), roles are bundles of permission sets, and delegation is accomplished via role-assignment resources scoped by environment and project tags.

1) Common delegation scenarios (concise):
- Scenario A: On-call engineer needs to rotate a GPU node in Dedicated for a single incident.
  - Principle: grant a scoped 'node-repair' temporary role tied to cluster-id and time-bound (1 hour). Use session tokens and require a Jira incident link in justification.
- Scenario B: Third-party contractor needs access to run performance evals on hosted test models only.
  - Principle: create 'contractor-eval' role scoped to the hosted-test-project and deny access to production models. Require MFA and audit-forwarding to customer SIEM (if customer-managed).
- Scenario C: SRE needs to read audit logs and trace spans for both hosted and dedicated customers but must not be able to modify model artifacts.
  - Principle: separate 'observability.read' from 'model.artifact.manage'. Provide cross-environment read roles with attribute-based filters (team==sre OR ticket==<id>).
- Scenario D: Customer admin for Private deployment must manage KMS keys and audit export settings inside their VPC.
  - Principle: provide a local 'private-admin' role that maps to customer-managed IAM (no Redwood control-plane privileges). Document onboarding checklist for key rotation, evidence export, and emergency contact.

2) Compact IAM role matrix (text table):
Columns: Role | Core permissions (high-level) | Hosted scope | Dedicated scope | Private scope | Typical delegation pattern
- infra-admin | infra.* (create clusters, scale) | Redwood-managed clusters only | customer-dedicated clusters (scoped by pool) | not applicable unless co-managed | delegated to Platform team via org policy, requires approval
- model-deployer | model.upload, model.deploy, model.rollback | allowed (limited to approved catalog) | allowed (customer-licensed models) | allowed (local artifacts) | deploys gated by model-signing + canary policies
- observability-reader | logs.read, traces.read, metrics.read | global (redwood) | local cluster logs (read-only) | local audit logs (read-only) | long-term role for SRE; access via ephemeral session
- node-repair | infra.node.* (reboot, drain) | not used | allowed (scoped to cluster-id) | allowed (if customer requests) | short-lived, incident-justified delegation
- billing-viewer | billing.usage.read | hosted usage only | dedicated usage for contracted pools | billing exported to customer billing system | read-only, used by finance and customer success

3) Role inheritance and RBAC v2 notes (practical):
- Avoid deep role inheritance chains. Use permission set composition instead (permission sets are single-level objects that are assembled into roles).
- Attribute-based scope: require roles to include 'environment' (hosted|dedicated|private) and 'project' or 'cluster_id' attributes. Enforcement layer must reject role bindings without the required attributes.
- Delegation flow: RoleOwner -> creates roleBinding(resource: roleBinding, attributes) -> audited issuance with justification_id -> session token minted with TTL.

4) Example policy templates (copyable) - Hosted, Dedicated, Private notes and minimal JSON examples (paste into IAM system).

(1) Hosted: short-lived operator role to touch model metadata but not artifacts
{
  "version": "1",
  "statement": [
    {"action": ["model.metadata.read", "model.metadata.update"], "resource": ["resource:hosted:models:catalog/*"], "effect": "allow"},
    {"action": ["model.artifact.*"], "resource": ["resource:hosted:models:catalog/*"], "effect": "deny"}
  ]
}

Notes: Hosted policies should reference hosted resource namespaces; deny statements are critical to prevent accidental artifact writes.

(2) Dedicated: node repair with cluster scoping and incident justification
{
  "version": "1",
  "statement": [
    {"action": ["infra.node.reboot", "infra.node.drain"], "resource": ["resource:dedicated:clusters:cluster-1234:nodes/*"], "condition": {"stringEquals": {"request:justification_ticket": "JIRA-\\d+"}}, "effect": "allow"}
  ]
}

Notes: The enforcement engine must validate the justification_ticket format. The role binding should be time-limited.

(3) Private: KMS admin template for customer-managed keys (note: this is translated to local IAM during onboarding)
{
  "version": "1",
  "statement": [
    {"action": ["kms:key:encrypt", "kms:key:decrypt", "kms:key:rotate"], "resource": ["resource:private:kms:customer-abc:keys/*"], "effect": "allow"}
  ]
}

Notes: For Private deployments Redwood operates only as a consultative role; the template is provided to customers to import into their KMS/IAM.

5) Audit log schema mapping and SIEM export (practical):
- Goal: guarantee that every role binding, temporary session creation, policy mutation, and admin operation produces an auditable event with consistent fields so SIEM rules can detect privilege escalation and evidence bundles can be produced automatically.
- Minimal event schema (flat key-value fields):
  - event_id (string)
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - actor_id (user:<id> | service:<id>)
  - actor_display_name
  - actor_roles (comma-separated list)
  - action (string, e.g., iam.bind_role, model.deploy, infra.node.reboot)
  - resource (resource string)
  - resource_type (e.g., model, cluster, node, kms)
  - environment (hosted|dedicated|private)
  - outcome (success|failure)
  - justification_id (optional, ticket link)
  - session_id (if temporary session)
  - ip_address
  - request_payload (truncated base64 or hash)
  - response_code
  - trace_id

- Sample log line (JSON blob for SIEM):
{
  "event_id": "ev-20240905-0001",
  "timestamp": "2024-09-05T14:22:31Z",
  "actor_id": "user:akhan",
  "actor_display_name": "Aisha Khan",
  "actor_roles": "observability-reader, temp-node-repair",
  "action": "infra.node.drain",
  "resource": "resource:dedicated:clusters:cluster-1234:nodes/node-17",
  "resource_type": "node",
  "environment": "dedicated",
  "outcome": "success",
  "justification_id": "JIRA-3456",
  "session_id": "s-0a1b2c",
  "ip_address": "34.82.19.201",
  "request_payload": "sha256:abc123...",
  "response_code": "200",
  "trace_id": "trace-77b"
}

SIEM export tips:
- Use structured JSON lines (one event per line) and gzip the export for long retention buckets.
- Tag events with environment and customer_id when possible so alert rules can be environment-specific.
- For Private deployments, provide a local forwarder template (rsyslog/FluentD) that maps local audit fields to the minimal event schema above.

6) Evidence automation runbook (checklist + flow):
- Trigger points: quarterly compliance snapshot, customer audit request, or suspicious escalation detection from SIEM.
- Data sources to include: roleBindings, policy versions, session issuance logs, audit event stream (last N days), KMS key rotation history (if applicable), model-signing attestations, and the canary rollout logs for any model deploys in scope.
- Packaging steps:
  1) Accept scope and timeframe (e.g., customer: ACME, timeframe: 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31).
  2) Query event store for all audit events where environment in scope and actor_roles includes admin-like roles.
  3) Export roleBindings and policy snapshots (store in read-only artifact bundle).
  4) Redact PII and include hashes of request_payloads rather than full payloads unless requested.
  5) Generate a markdown summary with findings and attach CSV timelines (event_id, timestamp, actor, action, resource, outcome).
  6) Seal bundle into an immutable S3 (or customer-provided) location with tamper-evidence metadata and sign the bundle.

Automation hints:
- Implement a single automation that takes an audit_scope input (customer, env, start, end) and emits the sealed bundle. Store run metadata (who requested, justification ticket) as part of the bundle.
- Leverage the session_id field to reconstruct the full chain of operations for short-lived privileged sessions.

7) Operational guardrails and acceptance criteria for onboarding Dedicated/Private:
- Dedicated onboarding: require at least one test incident drill where node-repair delegation is used and evidence is collected and verified.
- Private onboarding: verify forwarding of audit events to the customer SIEM or validated local forwarder; confirm KMS rotation policy is in place and documented.
- All onboarding must include a signed responsibilities matrix (who owns evidence retention, who responds to SIEM alerts, escalation path).

8) Open questions and follow-ups (working items):
- Should we require ILM (index lifecycle) policies on SIEM indices that contain role binding records older than X months? Proposal: 24 months default for privileged operations, 90 days for read-only observation logs.
- How to represent combined multi-role sessions in RBAC v2 UI without exploding the role graph? Prototype: present active session as union-of-permissions but show origin roleBindings and ticket links.
- Define a cross-team automation for proof-of-rotation of model-signing keys tied to deploys (link deploy -> signing_key_id).

Appendix: quick checklist for PR reviewers when approving role/policy changes:
- Is the scope attribute present and non-empty for any role binding?
- Is there an explicit deny for write/artifact operations when only metadata write is intended?
- Is the TTL on temporary role bindings <= 4 hours by default? If longer, is there an approval ticket?
- Are SIEM mapping fields (event_id, session_id, justification_id) being populated by the change?

End of working doc.

Notes on provenance: This is intentionally a pragmatic, operationally-focused doc and not the canonical policy. Convert items that reach consensus into the formal RBAC v2 spec and the compliance SOPs.
